title: Ratnapīṭha & Puṇḍravardhana
note: Ratnapīṭha is a later sacred-geography division; Puṇḍravardhana is a city, region and changing administrative province. Their North Bengal associations are shown together, but identical boundaries or universally interchangeable names are not established.

events.title: Puṇḍravardhana under Gupta officials
events.summary: The Damodarpur series records administration in Puṇḍravardhana-bhukti. It establishes Gupta provincial evidence, not the date when all of Ratnapīṭha was taken from Kamarupa.
events.limit: The dated documents do not prove identical Ratnapīṭha boundaries or a continuous transfer narrative.

events.title: A western acquisition attributed to Bhutivarman
events.summary: Some historical reconstructions place expansion into parts of Puṇḍravardhana around Bhutivarman’s time. This is the proposed acquisition episode, not a directly dated conquest charter.
events.limit: The Badganga and renewed grant evidence do not directly narrate conquest of the whole province; the geography and dating are debated.

events.title: Gauḍa campaign and proposed North Bengal control
events.summary: Bhaskaravarman’s camp at Karnasuvarna is directly attested. Wider possession of Puṇḍravardhana is a separate historical reconstruction, not a boundary supplied by that camp formula.
events.limit: This does not establish the acquisition date, recovery of a precisely defined Ratnapīṭha, or uninterrupted possession.

events.title: Puṇḍravardhana and Kāmarūpa are described separately
events.summary: The itinerary travels east from Puṇḍravardhana across a large river to Kamarupa. This geographic description must be read alongside, rather than erased by, reconstructions of Bhaskaravarman’s western campaigns.
events.limit: Separate descriptions are not by themselves a dated record of defeat or loss by Kamarupa.

events.date: Eighth century · identification and date vary
events.title: Gauḍa named in Harshadeva’s title
events.summary: The Paśupati inscription’s regional lordship title supplies another western-reach claim. It does not explicitly say that Ratnapīṭha or Puṇḍravardhana was recovered.
events.limit: A royal title is not converted into a dated reconquest or an administrative province boundary.

events.title: A proposed renewed North Bengal connection
events.summary: Historians have used Vanamala’s grant geography to reconstruct authority in Puṇḍravardhana or North Bengal. This proposed reassertion is included in the timeline with the identification dispute visible.
events.limit: The place identifications are contested; the record does not explicitly announce recovery of a lost Ratnapīṭha.

events.title: A victory in Gauḍa and an advance towards the Ganges
events.summary: Gachtal verse 15 reports the defeat of Rajyapala of Gauḍa. It is relevant to western influence, but an explicit recapture of Puṇḍravardhana or Ratnapīṭha is not stated.
events.limit: A campaign report cannot establish ownership of the whole province between recorded events.

events.title: A Bengal-Pāla charter names Puṇḍravardhana-bhukti
events.summary: The Belwa plate of Vigrahapala III, regnal year 11, records a grant within Puṇḍravardhana-bhukti. This is direct evidence of Bengal-Pāla administrative activity in the province.
events.limit: The year window is for orientation, not a fixed absolute conversion or proof that the whole sacred region changed hands at that date.

events.actor: Jatavarman of Bengal; Kamarupa ruler uncertain
events.title: A loss in Puṇḍravardhana attributed to Jatavarman
events.summary: Some historians read the Belava charter’s praise of Jatavarman as evidence that he took a portion of Puṇḍravardhana from Kamarupa. The reported loss is included, without assigning a securely known year or defeated Kamarupa king.
events.limit: Sharma questions the political reading of the Kama/rupa wording. It is therefore not shown as a confirmed loss of all Ratnapīṭha.
